about: Decoy replies for the judge's leniency check: each cites the right code but makes the wrong point, so the judge must not pass it on the named line. Written 13 Nov, before any judge run on them.

decoys.line: Finds that remove() mutates the list it was given (splice on list.items)
decoys.reply: [{"id": "d", "severity": "minor", "text": "remove() calls splice on list.items, which is O(n) for each removal; a filter would read better and scale the same, so prefer filter for speed on long lists.", "where": "src/reading-list.ts:42"}]

decoys.line: Finds that remove() mutates the list it was given (splice on list.items)
decoys.reply: [{"id": "d", "severity": "minor", "text": "In remove(), the return value of list.items.splice(index, 1) is ignored and the item is read separately with list.items[index]; use the spliced element instead to avoid the extra lookup.", "where": "src/reading-list.ts:41"}]

decoys.line: Finds that remove() mutates the list it was given (splice on list.items)
decoys.reply: [{"id": "d", "severity": "minor", "text": "remove() uses splice on list.items, which is the right call here: it keeps the other items' order, and the PR's tests pass, so nothing needs to change.", "where": "src/reading-list.ts:42"}]
